audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..3].side read 'Skill' while win[0..3] and packet.levelChart all read 'Anivia'.
audit.why: Four of seven rows rendered two different answers, and they contradicted the content layer's own whys, which explain in detail why Anivia is ahead from level 3.
audit.corrected: Full-layer chart aligned to Anivia for the first four rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike or cooldown line carries Destiny's real numbers.
audit.why: Destiny is 170/140/110s with 5500 range and reveals every enemy champion before the 1.5s Gate. The gap between a Destiny that is up and one that is spent is the only real power swing in this lane.
audit.corrected: 170s and the 1.5s Gate channel written into the do's, don'ts and cooldown lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer treats Pick a Card as an ability that lands on its own, and never states the delivery condition.
audit.why: Pick a Card (6s, 200 range) only selects the card — the stun arrives on a BASIC ATTACK, and it is an auto-reset (flagged in missingInteractions). Anivia's Frostbite reaches 650 and Flash Frost 1075, so correct spacing means the gold card never touches her. Wild Cards, by contrast, damages every unit it passes through, so standing behind the wave does not stop it.
audit.corrected: Gold card described as auto-delivered with the wind-up as the tell; Wild Cards described as piercing.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. It governs your forward steps. - W Crystallize spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Pick a Card is only 6s, but the gold card reaches you on a basic attack — stay outside auto range and it never lands. - Wild Cards is 6s and damages everything it passes through, so hiding behind the wave does nothing. - Destiny is 170s at rank 1 and reveals your whole team.

edits.before: Make him kill you twice through a stun and a wall — then storm the wave he stopped farming. Nothing here works through Pick a Card (Gold) — schedule your pattern around its cooldown.
edits.after: Make him kill you twice through a stun and a wall — then storm the wave he stopped farming. His gold card has to arrive on an auto-attack, so spacing rather than cooldown counting is the whole defence.

edits.before: Twisted Fate wins by landing Pick a Card (Gold), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by Gating in behind you on Destiny and landing the gold-card auto while your stun is on cooldown.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Twisted Fate burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Step up while his card is unlocked: Flash Frost for the chill, E for double damage, and stay outside auto range so the gold card has nothing to land on.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Twisted Fate walks straight at you.
edits.after: Standing inside his auto range with a card locked — that stun is delivered by a basic attack, and everything else follows it.

edits.before: Good trade: Threaten Q until Twisted Fate burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade. Bad trade: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Twisted Fate walks straight at you.
edits.after: Good trade: Step up while his card is unlocked: Flash Frost for the chill, E for double damage, and stay outside auto range so the gold card has nothing to land on. Bad trade: Standing inside his auto range with a card locked — that stun is delivered by a basic attack, and everything else follows it.

edits.before: If Twisted Fate gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Pick a Card (Gold) extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Twisted Fate gets a kill he converts it into map pressure rather than lane pressure — track Destiny and ping every roam. Two kills: farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by owning the ground he Gates onto: storm the pit, and a wall on his landing spot turns his flank into a free stun.

edits.before: The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: The gold card is delivered by an auto-attack: the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the moment the card glows yellow.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Twisted Fate burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Destiny's Gate is a 1.5-second channel with a visible cast — wall the ground he lands on and he arrives inside your storm with no way out.

edits.before: Twisted Fate spends Pick a Card (Gold) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Destiny is 170s at rank 1 — once it is spent, the map stops being a gank and the lane is just yours.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Wild Cards damages everything it passes through and is up every 6s — you cannot hide behind the wave.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Twisted Fate walks straight at you.
edits.after: Destiny reveals your whole team at 5500 range, so a fight away from tower is a fight his jungler already knows about.

notes: packet.suspectNames flags 'Gold Card' as a probable wrong name matching 'Wild Cards' — that is a false positive. Gold Card is the correct in-game name for the stun variant of Pick a Card, and the surrounding text (spikes[1], whys[4]) uses it correctly; left untouched. Level chart: content win[0..6] already matched packet.levelChart; only the full layer's first four rows read 'Skill', so those edits remove an existing disagreement. The content layer for this matchup is already specific and non-templated, so no content edits were needed — all the templating was on the full layer. Ratings left at 5/10 on the flipped rows since the rating scale's meaning was not clear enough to change safely.
